_about: Linux sim racing tools worth knowing, curated from the community index awesome-linux-simracing and the projects themselves.

community.name: Sim Racing on Linux
community.what: Community hub: Discord, Matrix chat, Reddit and a wiki for help with setups.

community.name: r/simracingonlinux
community.what: Reddit community for Linux sim racing questions and setups.

community.name: SROL community racing
community.what: Sim Racing on Linux's own Assetto Corsa server, with live timing.

community.name: awesome-linux-simracing
community.what: Community index of Linux sim racing software.

community.name: linux-steering-wheels
community.what: Tested force feedback support table for wheels on Linux.

tools.name: linux-simracing-utils
tools.what: One installer for SimHub and CrewChief on Linux, with telemetry bridging via winecarte.
tools.steamos: Runs from Desktop Mode; a good choice if you need SimHub dashboards or CrewChief's spotter.

tools.name: winecarte
tools.what: Mirrors Proton games' shared memory into /dev/shm via a launch option. Pitwall installs it for you.

tools.name: Datalink
tools.what: Launch-option wrapper that maps shared memory for AC/ACC/EVO, AMS2/PC2, rF2, RaceRoom and ETS2/ATS.
tools.steamos: Needs building from source (Rust) or the AUR.

tools.name: simshmbridge
tools.what: Bridge executables for AC/ACC and PC2/AMS2; can also map Linux memory back into another prefix.

tools.name: Boxflat
tools.what: Full MOZA settings app for Linux (Pitwall's MOZA protocol comes from it).

tools.name: Oversteer
tools.what: Settings for Logitech, Thrustmaster and Fanatec wheels.

tools.name: monocoque
tools.what: Bass shakers, tachometers, sim lights and Arduino devices from telemetry.

tools.name: acctelemetry
tools.what: Telemetry graphs from MoTeC files, designed for ACC.

tools.name: protopedal
tools.what: Virtual devices to merge or fix pedals and wheels that games don't detect properly.

tools.name: Content Manager (AC)
tools.what: Guide to running Assetto Corsa's Content Manager under Proton.

tools.name: SimMonitor
tools.what: Telemetry dashboards in the terminal, a web browser or on a small screen, by the author of Monocoque.
tools.steamos: Desktop Mode; Pitwall's phone dashboard covers the same need in Gaming Mode.

tools.name: simracing-hwdb
tools.what: Community collection of udev hwdb entries so wheels, pedals and shifters are seen as joysticks.
tools.steamos: Pitwall's Fix wheel and pedal detection writes an equivalent entry for the devices you have plugged in.
